pages.text: The sun changes from day to day: $(thing)great, good, average, fair, poor$() or a $(thing)blackout$(). Each condition rates every HF band good, fair, poor or closed, by day and by night, and sets the static level. In a blackout HF is dead.$(br2)A $(l:radiocraft:digital/teletype)teletype$(/l) next to a radio with a real antenna prints the report from its blue SOLAR WX lamp, and a comparator on it reads 1 (blackout) to 6 (great).

A blackout may bring an $(thing)aurora$() a few days later, lighting the sky far north or south (Z beyond 10000). Under it VHF skips 500 to 4000 blocks with a raspy buzz, while HF gets worse and noisier.
pages.title: Aurora
